data.name: PING 1.5+™
data.detailed_description:
Everyone on the block is playing this game!

PING 1.5+™ is a new arcade style puzzle game with the objective of shooting the cube through over 100 stages to reach the orange. Get frustrated in trying to beat all of the stages; this game isn't for the weakhearted. PING 1.5+™ mimics the retro days of gaming by having a notoriously hard difficulty curve.

PING™ is on a mission to save the world against the Spheres. Will he succeed? Only you can decide the world's fate with your "ultimate master super gaming" skills.

Game Features

  • Over 100 levels
  • Original soundtrack by Elkskin
  • Retro 3D visuals
  • HARD

reviews.review:
PING 1.5+ is a compact arcade puzzle game that takes a remarkably simple idea and turns it into a demanding test of precision, timing, and spatial awareness. Developed and published by Nami Tentou, it avoids unnecessary complexity and instead builds its identity around launching a cube through obstacle-filled stages toward a designated goal. It is the kind of game that can be understood within minutes but takes considerably longer to master, particularly once the layouts begin demanding increasingly accurate movements.

The central mechanic revolves around controlling PING, a cube that must reach an orange target. Movement is handled more like launching an object than freely navigating a traditional platforming character. Because of this, every attempt requires the player to think about direction, distance, obstacles, and the consequences of committing to a particular move. Early stages establish the rules without overwhelming the player, while later challenges expect increasingly careful execution. What initially feels like a basic arcade mechanic eventually becomes a surprisingly effective foundation for puzzle solving.

With more than 100 levels, the game manages to stretch this concept across a substantial campaign. The environments gradually become more complicated, introducing situations where blindly launching toward the destination is unlikely to work. Players need to observe the geometry of each area, identify potential routes, and then execute their plan accurately. Failure is common, but retries are an intentional part of the experience. The satisfaction comes from gradually understanding a troublesome stage and finally completing a sequence that previously seemed impossible.

Difficulty is one of the game's defining characteristics. PING 1.5+ openly embraces an old-school approach where repeated failure is expected rather than carefully avoided. This can create some genuinely rewarding victories, especially after spending several attempts learning a difficult section. At the same time, it means the game will not appeal equally to everyone. Players looking for a relaxed puzzle experience may find the increasing precision requirements frustrating, whereas those who enjoy overcoming difficult mechanical challenges are more likely to appreciate its design philosophy.

The campaign also includes multiple worlds and boss encounters, helping break up what could otherwise have become a repetitive sequence of isolated puzzles. Bosses are an interesting addition because they apply the familiar mechanics in situations that feel more significant than an ordinary stage. Progressing into new areas gives the game a clearer structure and provides tangible milestones as the difficulty rises. Steam achievements further complement this progression, particularly for players interested in completing every challenge rather than simply reaching the ending.

Its visual presentation follows a minimalist retro-inspired 3D style dominated by geometric forms. The graphics are functional rather than spectacular, but that simplicity benefits gameplay because obstacles and objectives remain easy to distinguish. There is little visual clutter to distract from calculating a movement or identifying a safe route. The aesthetic also gives the game an appropriately arcade-like personality, making its straightforward presentation feel intentional rather than merely limited.

The soundtrack adds some much-needed energy to the otherwise minimal presentation. Since difficult stages may require numerous attempts, music plays an important role in maintaining momentum while the player repeatedly experiments with different approaches. The audio and visuals work together to create an experience reminiscent of classic arcade games, where a relatively small collection of mechanics could provide considerable entertainment through increasingly difficult variations.

There is a lightweight story involving PING and a conflict with the Spheres, although narrative is clearly secondary to gameplay. This is a sensible choice because an elaborate storyline could easily interrupt the rapid cycle of attempting a stage, failing, adjusting the strategy, and trying again. The playful premise instead gives the abstract cube and geometric environments some personality without demanding that players spend significant amounts of time away from the actual challenges.

The largest weakness comes from the same philosophy that gives the game its appeal. Its simplicity means that players who do not become invested in mastering the launching mechanic may find the overall experience repetitive. There are many levels, but they remain variations on a focused central idea rather than introducing entirely new genres or complicated progression systems. Difficulty spikes can also make certain sections feel more frustrating than rewarding. Patience is therefore almost as important as mechanical skill.

On Steam Deck, PING 1.5+ does not have an official Valve Verified or Playable compatibility rating, so its Steam Deck status should be considered Unknown or Unverified. The game is relatively lightweight and its straightforward controls may make experimentation through Proton possible, but the absence of an official compatibility classification means Deck users should not assume a completely tested handheld experience.

Overall, PING 1.5+ is an enjoyable example of how a minimalist mechanic can support a surprisingly substantial challenge. Its more than 100 levels, multiple worlds, bosses, achievements, retro presentation, and emphasis on precision give it enough substance to keep determined players occupied. It is deliberately demanding and occasionally frustrating, but overcoming that difficulty is precisely where much of its satisfaction comes from. Players who enjoy straightforward arcade puzzle games built around repetition, experimentation, and eventual mastery should find plenty to appreciate.

Rating: 7/10
